why_this_exists: docs/live-tool-transcript.json records `existing_incident_urns` running twice live and returning {} both times, because every cycle in that capture began from a full reset. So the URN-addressed `save_document` overwrite in cure.py -- the fix for the duplicate-incident bug -- had never actually executed against a real GMS. Of the 34 live `save_document` calls in that transcript, the only 4 carrying a `urn` are KB-document cures, not incident records. This cycle closes that gap.
method: Starting from the cured graph left by the hijack A/B run, delete the datasets and the two poisoned KB documents -- so the corpus can be re-planted on entities that no longer carry `injection-quarantined` and the sweep will look at them again -- but KEEP the 12 `antigen-incident-*` records. Re-seed, then cure again. The second cure's `existing_incident_urns` therefore resolves a non-empty ledger and every incident save is addressed by the existing record's URN.

result.verdict: PASS -- 12 records in, 12 records out, all 12 URNs unchanged. The overwrite branch executed. Before the fix this cycle would have minted a second record per cured locus.

honest_caveat: The second cure defused 11 loci, not 12: one of the two KB-document payloads had not re-indexed in OpenSearch when the sweep ran (the same asynchronous-index behaviour DEMO.md already documents, and the sweep reported `1 documents` rather than 2). So 11 of the 12 records were rewritten in place this cycle and the 12th was simply not touched. The claim the count supports is exactly this: no duplicate record was minted for any locus that WAS re-cured. It does not claim all 12 were rewritten.
